Short no-via RP2354 internal-regulator switch path.
Direct TPS564252 bootstrap hot-side connection.

Tapered no-via TPS564252 SW path, widened after clearing the adjacent 0.5-mm-pitch pins.

BQ25798 SW1 leaves the fine pad on B.Cu, fans through three standard vias to a short 0.6-mm In2.Cu crossing, and returns through three vias into a 0.8-mm inductor stub; no via is placed in an SMD pad.
BQ25798 SW2 mirrors SW1 on In3.Cu so the two current paths may cross without sharing copper; six standard through vias provide parallel current paths and remain outside the SMD pads.
The low-current BTST1 capacitor return uses one standard via to join the already reviewed In2.Cu SW1 branch, as allowed by the BQ25798 layout guidance.
The low-current BTST2 capacitor return uses one standard via to join the already reviewed In3.Cu SW2 branch, as allowed by the BQ25798 layout guidance.
Direct no-via B.Cu connection from BQ25798 PMID to the relocated 0.1-uF C8; the narrow pad escape widens immediately while staying below the package corner pad.
Direct no-via B.Cu connection from BQ25798 SYS to the relocated 0.1-uF C16, symmetric with the PMID high-frequency path.
Same-layer wide copper fans the already local 0.1-uF PMID node into all three bulk capacitors without adding inductive vias to the high-frequency path.
Short same-layer widening connects the SYS high-frequency capacitor to the complete bulk bank before the protected system rail leaves the charger island.
The BQ25798 REGN bypass capacitor is connected directly on B.Cu with a short pad escape that clears the adjacent package pins and widens at the capacitor.
Two short standard through vias give the mandatory PMID 0.1-uF capacitor a low-inductance return into the future uninterrupted ground planes without using via-in-pad.
Two short standard through vias give the mandatory SYS 0.1-uF capacitor a low-inductance return into the future uninterrupted ground planes without using via-in-pad.
The REGN bypass ground receives two ordinary through-via returns at the outside edge of its large pad, leaving the capacitor replaceable and avoiding filled-via processing.
The two accessible BQ25798 ground pins are joined locally and each receives its own standard through via into the inner reference planes.
The rotated input capacitor presents its NVDC_SYS pad directly to both TPS629203 VIN pins; the route widens after clearing MODE/S-CONF.
Wide copper connects the inductor to the rotated output capacitor; the TPS629203 output-sense pin reaches that quiet capacitor node around, not through, the switch copper.
The shifted TPS629203 ground pin reaches one standard through via in the real inter-package corridor; an inner-layer local return continues directly to the input-capacitor via pair.
The AON input capacitor ground enters the inner reference plane through two ordinary vias immediately outside its large pad.
The AON output capacitor ground enters the inner reference plane through two ordinary vias immediately outside its large pad.
Both TPS566231P VIN pins join first, then reach the 0.1-uF input capacitor directly on B.Cu with immediate widening and no via.
A short 1.5-mm output trunk feeds the two capacitors beside the 6-A inductor; the third capacitor joins through a separate left-side branch that avoids both intervening ground pads.
The regulator ground pin joins the VCC bypass return locally and reaches the inner reference plane through a standard via in the gap between the two bulk-input pads.
The 0.1-uF input capacitor receives two ordinary through-via returns and joins the regulator ground skeleton directly on the first inner layer.
All three output-capacitor ground pads receive paired ordinary vias; a short inner-layer skeleton joins them to each other and to the same local regulator return.
The bias supply escapes below the VCC pin, crosses the three left-side pin fan-outs on the outer face, and returns immediately to the dedicated bypass capacitor without entering the switch-node area.
The feedback pin, divider midpoint and feed-forward capacitor share one quiet B.Cu branch routed outside the VCC and switch-node fan-outs.
A narrow Kelvin branch senses the output at the left capacitor-bank junction and reaches both parallel top-divider elements without carrying load current.
The bottom-divider resistor receives its own ordinary via and joins the output-capacitor ground skeleton without crossing the feedback trace on B.Cu.

The three bulk input capacitors join the already-direct high-frequency input node through paired standard vias and a 1.0-mm In2 power spine, keeping load-current copper away from feedback and the switch-node face.
Both upper bulk capacitors receive paired ordinary ground vias, while the side capacitor joins the existing high-frequency return pair; all three close into the same In1 local ground skeleton.
The direct and bulk input capacitors join VIN through paired standard vias and a compact In2 spine; the high-frequency branch stays separate from the switch-node escape on B.Cu.
The IC, high-frequency capacitor, bulk capacitor and bottom feedback resistor share one short In1 return skeleton with ordinary, non-via-in-pad stitching.
A short 1.5-mm output trunk fans directly from the inductor into the two local 22-uF capacitors without a via.
Both output capacitors receive paired ordinary ground vias and join the input/IC return through the same local In1 skeleton.
The divider midpoint crosses the switch-node escape only on F.Cu over the In1 reference, then returns beside the top divider and feed-forward capacitor; no feedback copper shares the In2 power spine.
A narrow Kelvin branch leaves the right output-capacitor junction, bypasses the unrelated fuse on In3, and feeds both parallel top-divider elements without carrying load current.
The relocated 0.1-uF capacitor connects directly to VIN without a via, then widens into the adjacent bulk input capacitor below the regulator.
The regulator, direct input capacitor, bulk capacitor and relocated bottom-divider ground close into one ordinary-via In1 return skeleton.
Two separate 0.8-mm no-via branches leave the inductor output pad for the upper and lower bulk capacitors without entering the switch-node side.
Both output capacitors receive paired ordinary ground vias and join the same local In1 return used by the regulator and input bank.
The quiet feedback spine stays on B.Cu, links both divider bottoms, and reaches the relocated bottom resistor without sharing a power-current segment.
A narrow Kelvin branch senses the upper output capacitor, crosses below the cell on In3, and feeds both top-divider elements without carrying load current.

Two ordinary vias feed both ends of the eFuse IN bar from a 1.2-mm internal trunk; two source-side vias join the existing converter output bank, while the divider feed remains a narrow branch rather than carrying load current.

A short dogbone leaves the otherwise enclosed dVdt pin; the quiet In2 bridge reaches the nearby timing capacitor without a via in either component pad.
The complete OVLO divider uses the otherwise empty outer face as a quiet bridge; all three vias sit outside solder-pad drill areas and the branch stays separate from the power trunk.
The PGTH divider uses a separate outer-face branch around the output capacitor and rejoins both resistor ends without crossing the OVLO bridge or the eFuse ground island.
All seven local eFuse ground terminals join a quiet In1 island; one 0.8-mm star branch reaches the existing system-ground skeleton below the mezzanine without carrying main-rail load current.
The rotated eFuse input pair now faces the converter output; its direct bypass and OVLO-divider feed join the same raw rail without burdening the quiet divider branch with load current.
The protected AON output reaches its local bulk capacitor through a short two-via In2 bridge around the ILIM resistor, keeping unlike surface nets separated.
The complete OVLO divider joins the control pin through a narrow In3 bridge so it does not cross the protected-output escape on the component layer.
The current-limit programming resistor has a direct, quiet surface connection after the eFuse orientation correction.
The eFuse exposed pad and ground pin, both local capacitors and both programming-resistor returns receive a joined ordinary-via In1 return tied into the existing AON converter ground skeleton.
